classifier_rationale: The customer bought one $89 print but was charged $267.00 for three, a posted amount that differs from the agreed purchase, so this is a wrong amount.

retrieved.text: Written notice link. After a billing-error intake by phone, send the cardholder a link the same day to submit or confirm the dispute electronically. The cardholder's submission is the written notice under REG-03. The call alone is not. POL-04 does not apply to UN, because notice of unauthorized use can be by phone (REG-12).

What counts as a billing error. A charge the cardholder didn't authorize; a charge that isn't identified properly; goods or services not accepted or not delivered as agreed; a payment or credit not posted properly; a computational error by the issuer; a request for clarification or documentation about a charge; failure to send a statement to the last known address.

Fraud routing. Any charge the cardholder says they didn't make or authorize goes to the fraud team on the same call. Block the card, reissue, open a fraud claim. Agents do not open these as billing disputes only.

note: Cardholder reports a $267.00 charge from Paperloom Studio dated 2026-09-19, posted on the 2026-09-29 statement. Cardholder says they ordered one art print for $89.00 and received one print. The packing slip listed quantity one, but the charge reflects three prints. Cardholder emailed the merchant last week with a photo of the packing slip and has not heard back. Disputed difference: $178.00. Call is 16 days after the statement, within the 60-day window. Intent WA, next action OPEN_DISPUTE: send the written-notice link the same day per POL-04, billing error per REG-01. Temp credit eligible (under $250). Unknown: any merchant response, whether the cardholder has sent written notice to the card issuer, and whether other charges are involved. No second issue raised.
